title: The Oct 10-11 2025 crypto deleveraging crash - the largest liquidation event in crypto history (~$19B+), the Trump-tariff trigger, the Hyperliquid perp cascade, and the USDe depeg
source: Public record + market data (Coinglass, CoinDesk, CoinShares, KuCoin, Reuters), Oct 10-11 2025: a ~$19.1B 24-hour liquidation wave - Coinglass designated it the LARGEST liquidation event in crypto history - ~$16.7B of it longs, ~1.6M trader accounts wiped; Coinglass later said the true nominal total was likely $30-40B once slower-reporting exchanges (Binance, Bybit data-feed disruptions) were folded in. Trigger: President Trump's announcement of a 100% tariff on Chinese imports (Fri Oct 10 2025) reignited trade tensions; equities/commodities sold off and cross-asset deleveraging hit crypto. Price impact: Bitcoin fell ~14% from a ~$122,574 Friday high to a ~$104,783 low; Ether -12.2% to ~$3,436; total crypto market cap fell ~$400B (~$4.15T -> ~$3.74T). Perpetual-futures open interest across major venues dropped ~43% ($217B -> $123B) in a day; the largest contraction was Hyperliquid, where OI fell ~57% ($14B -> $6B) and a ~$203M ETH/USDT long was liquidated - the largest DEX liquidation ever recorded. Secondary trigger: on Binance the synthetic-dollar stablecoin USDe briefly fell to ~$0.65, forcing further liquidations across liquid-staking tokens, alt-L1s, and derivatives. Resilience: infrastructure mostly HELD - stablecoins broadly repegged, major exchanges processed billions in forced sales without failing, DeFi protocols liquidated bad loans without accumulating toxic debt. HONESTY/GRADE: the liquidation totals, price moves, OI contraction, the Hyperliquid record, and the USDe depeg are FACT (exchange + Coinglass data); the $30-40B 'true total' is a LABELED Coinglass estimate; the event is correctly dated Oct 2025 (carried as documented history, ~1yr before this entry). Both sides recorded: the crash exposed real fragility (hidden leverage, perp-DEX auto-deleveraging, oracle/stablecoin-depeg mechanics) AND the plumbing proved resilient (no 2022-style insolvency cascade). Cross-refs: spec-ethena-usde-synthetic-dollar (the USDe mechanism), spec-crypto-collapse-cluster (the 2022 contrast), macro-carry-trades + spec-unwind-timing (leverage unwind), spec-exchanges-asia (Binance). Overlay/structural market-event edges only; new nodes are isolated from the AI-financial SCC, which is unchanged.

edges.notes: TRIGGER: the Oct 10 2025 announcement of a 100% tariff on Chinese imports reignited trade tensions; equities/commodities sold off and cross-asset deleveraging cascaded into crypto. FACT of the trigger-and-timing; 'caused' is the proximate read (markets were already leverage-heavy).
Bitcoin fell ~14% from a ~$122,574 Friday high to a ~$104,783 low; total crypto market cap fell ~$400B (~$4.15T -> ~$3.74T) (fact).
Ether fell ~12.2% to ~$3,436 amid the forced unwind (fact).

The sharpest perp contraction: Hyperliquid open interest fell ~57% ($14B -> $6B) and a ~$203M ETH/USDT long was liquidated - the largest DEX liquidation ever recorded. Total perp OI across major venues dropped ~43% ($217B -> $123B) in a day (fact).

On Binance the synthetic-dollar stablecoin USDe briefly fell to ~$0.65; Binance/Bybit data-feed disruptions may have masked the full liquidation scale (Coinglass later estimated a $30-40B true total vs the $19.1B reported). FACT of the depeg + reported figures; the $30-40B is a labeled estimate.

SECONDARY TRIGGER: the USDe depeg to ~$0.65 on Binance forced further liquidations across liquid-staking tokens, alt-L1s, and derivatives - the synthetic-dollar fragility mapped in spec-ethena-usde-synthetic-dollar amplifying the cascade. USDe broadly repegged after (fact of the depeg + repeg; amplification read labeled).

The event was a PERPETUAL-FUTURES deleveraging above all: ~$19.1B liquidated in 24h (~$16.7B longs), ~1.6M accounts, 10-20x any prior liquidation day (April 2021 was ~$10B). The leverage, not spot selling, was the amplifier (fact; 'largest ever' is Coinglass's designation).

RESILIENCE SIDE (recorded for balance): infrastructure mostly held - stablecoins broadly repegged, major exchanges processed billions in forced sales without failing, and DeFi protocols liquidated bad loans without accumulating toxic debt - no 2022-style insolvency cascade (spec-crypto-collapse-cluster contrast). Fact of the resilience; the 'systemic vs idiosyncratic' verdict is contested.
